title: Smallest Covering Window
statement:
You have a long `text` and a short word `need`. A **window** is a stretch of consecutive letters of `text`. A window **covers** `need` if it contains every letter of `need`, as many times as that letter appears in `need` (extra letters in the window are fine).

Return the **length of the shortest window that covers `need`**, or `0` if no window does.
constraints: both strings contain only lowercase letters a-z

examples.explanation: The window banc contains a, b and c.
The text has only one a, but two are needed.

hints.nudge: Grow a window to the right until it covers `need`. Then, how can you make it smaller without breaking it?
hints.pattern: Sliding window with letter counts: expand the right end, then shrink the left end while the window still covers.
hints.walkthrough: Checking every window is O(n^2) windows times a check. Use two pointers. Keep a table of how many of each letter are still needed (it can go negative for extras) and a counter 'missing' of letters not yet covered. Move right one letter at a time. Whenever missing reaches 0 the window covers need: record its length, then move left forward to try to shrink it (if you remove a letter that was needed, missing goes up again and you stop shrinking). Each pointer moves at most n times, so O(n).
